{"notes":"CORRECTED 2026-11-23. Mark: "doesnt the spec have something already,
just weakly specified?" He is right, and my description above undersold
it. Read the actual text rather than characterising it.

WHAT MIMI-CONTENT-10 ACTUALLY HAS:

1. A NAMED SECTION: §5.10 "Conferencing" (txt line 1796).
2. The `session` disposition, value 7, in the IANA Content Disposition
   Values registry (§line 2326: "a description of a multimedia session,
   or URI"). Note it covers BOTH an SDP-style DESCRIPTION and a join
   URI; I had only noted the URI.
3. A COMPLETE WORKED EXAMPLE, lines 1804-1835: the CBOR of a
   conferencing message, topicId "Foo 118", an ExternalPart with
   disposition 7, cardinality 2 (external), url
   "https://example.com/join/12345", description "Join the Foo 118
   conference".
4. Two described approaches: the URL "could be rendered to the user,
   requiring a click. Alternatively the URL could be in an ExternalPart
   with a disposition of session, which could be processed differently
   by the client (for example, alerting the user or presenting a dialog
   box)."

AND THE SENTENCE THAT EXPLAINS THE WEAKNESS, §5.10: "Further discussion
of calling and conferencing functionality is out-of-scope of this
document."

So it is not an omission. It is an explicit scope boundary, and
everything inside it is "could", never MUST or SHOULD: nothing
interoperable is specified.

THIS ALSO VINDICATES MIMID'S CHOICES rather than making them inventions:
- Mapping a session part to a JMAP VTC MessageAction so the client can
  show a join affordance IS §5.10's "alerting the user or presenting a
  dialog box". mimid is implementing the spec's own suggestion.
- The never-fetch rule has implicit support in the example, which nulls
  every content-fetch field: expires 0, size 0, encAlg none, hashAlg
  none. A session ExternalPart is plainly not content to download.

CHECKED AND NOTHING FURTHER EXISTS: draft-mimi-content-more-extensions-01
covers sender timestamp, external message ID, subject and lastSeen
ordering. Nothing about calling.

SO THE WG POSTURE CHANGES, and for the better. Not "you forgot
something" but: §5.10 deliberately defers calling, here is what one
implementation had to decide in the gap, and here is the interop
consequence. Concretely, what two implementations cannot agree on
today while staying conformant:
- whether a session part is rendered as a link or acted on;
- which URL schemes carry (mimid takes https and wss);
- whether the DESCRIPTION form, the other half of the disposition's
  definition, is expected at all -- mimid handles only the URI form;
- what a receiver that cannot join does;
- lifetime, ringing, declining, who is present.

The question for the WG is whether calling should come into scope, and
mimid's implementation is the evidence for asking. Posting still needs
Mark's OK."}

{"notes":"ANSWERED DEFINITIVELY 2026-11-23, Mark asked whether we raised it in the
MIMI GitHub repos. Queried the repos themselves with gh rather than
inferring from local notes.

NO. We have 46 issues open or closed across the three repos as
MarkAtwood -- 6 on draft-ietf-mimi-content, 20 on mimi-protocol, 20 on
mimi-room-policy -- and not one is about conferencing, calling, a
session part or a VTC endpoint. A body search for
"conferencing OR conference OR calling OR vtc" across all three returns
nothing.

THE CLOSEST, and it is a genuinely useful find: mimi-room-policy #40,
"Parent-dependent rooms: strict subset vs the call-room note", Mark's
own and open. It is about the strict-subset rule, and it mentions calls
only because room-policy §5's note uses one as its example.

WHICH MEANS MIMI'S CALL STORY IS SPLIT ACROSS TWO DRAFTS THAT DO NOT
REFERENCE EACH OTHER, and that is the better observation to take to the
WG:

- mimi-content §5.10 has the SESSION: the `session` disposition, a join
  URI or a multimedia session description, a worked CBOR example -- then
  "Further discussion of calling and conferencing functionality is
  out-of-scope of this document."
- mimi-room-policy §5 (txt L542-544) has the CALL ROOM: "A room can be
  both fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used
  for a multi-media call of clients in a Group DM."

So the room model for a call is in room-policy and the session pointer is
in content, neither cites the other, and the document that would join
them declares the subject out of scope.

AND THE CALL-ROOM MODEL IS ALREADY BROKEN FOR THE OBVIOUS CASE, which
Mark's #40 found while implementing -04: §5 L533 requires a
parent-dependent room's participants to be a STRICT subset of the
parent's, so a call with everyone in the Group DM is forbidden; and
L530's "Only a single fixed-membership room can exist for any unique set
of participants" collides with it too. #40 suggests "subset" for "strict
subset" and exempting parent-dependent rooms from the single-room rule.
Unanswered.

SO THE POST TO MAKE, once Mark approves one: a mimi-content issue asking
whether calling comes into scope, pointing at room-policy's call-room
note as evidence the WG already assumes calls exist, at #40 as evidence
the room half does not work as written, and at mimid's implementation as
what one implementation had to decide in the gap. That is three pieces
of evidence rather than an opinion."}

{"design":"TITLE: §5.10: what is a receiver expected to do with a session part?

BODY:
This came out of implementing §5.10 in mimid, mapping MIMI messages onto
JMAP Chat. §5.10 and the `session` disposition give enough to send a
conference invitation, and the example is clear. What a receiver should
do with one is left open, and "Further discussion of calling and
conferencing functionality is out-of-scope of this document" means that
is deliberate — so this is a question about scope rather than a defect
report.

Four things mimid had to decide with nothing to read:

- Whether a session part is rendered as a link or acted on. §5.10 offers
  both ("rendered to the user, requiring a click" or "processed
  differently by the client, for example alerting the user"), which is
  fine for a client and not enough for two implementations to agree.
  mimid acts on it: it becomes a join affordance, not body text.
- Whether a session part is content to fetch. mimid never fetches one.
  The example implies that by leaving `size`, `expires`, `encAlg` and
  `hashAlg` at 0 or none, but it is not stated, and an implementation
  that treats every ExternalPart alike would try to download the URL.
- Which URL schemes are meaningful. mimid accepts `https` and `wss` and
  puts any other scheme in the body as text. That is a guess; a SIP URI
  seems equally intended, since §1 gives interoperating with SIP as a
  goal.
- The other half of the disposition. The registry says "a description of
  a multimedia session, or URI used to join one". mimid handles only the
  URI form. For the description form there is no stated content type or
  shape, so a sender using it reaches a receiver that cannot act on it.

There is also a second half of the story in another draft, which may be
worth joining up: room-policy §5 notes that "A room can be both
fixed_membership and parent_dependent, for example, for room used for a
multi-media call of clients in a Group DM". So the room model for a call
is in room-policy, the session pointer is in mimi-content, and neither
references the other. (Separately, I think room-policy's version does not
work for the obvious case — a call with everyone in the Group DM is not a
*strict* subset of it; that is ietf-wg-mimi/mimi-room-policy#40.)

The question: should calling and conferencing come into scope somewhere?
If not, would a sentence in §5.10 on what a receiver may assume — that a
session part is an endpoint rather than content, and what to do with a
scheme or a description form it cannot use — be in scope as interop
guidance without opening up calling itself?"}

   Secrets" -- a forward-secure exporter, SafeExportSecret(ComponentID),
   one secret per app component, consumed and the source material
   deleted. Generic "for use by application components"; calls are not
   named, and §4.1 makes a ComponentID application-scoped, so it is the
   application's to assign.

   plus parent_dependent.

media component.

machinery that all exists, and no two implementations would agree,

with a session part"), and it reframes §5.10's out-of-scope sentence:

expected.
